html:
Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers. On the map it covers British Southern Rhodesia and the republic that won independence in 1980.

The name comes from Great Zimbabwe, the stone city the Shona built from the 11th century. In 1890 Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company sent settlers into Mashonaland. It crushed the Ndebele in 1893 and a Shona and Ndebele rising in 1896 to 1897.

  • 1923: Southern Rhodesia became a self-governing colony run by its white minority.
  • 1965: Ian Smith declared independence to block Black majority rule. A long guerrilla war followed.
  • 1980: independence as Zimbabwe, with Robert Mugabe in power.
  • 1983 to 1987: army massacres in Matabeleland killed thousands.
  • 2000: fast-track land reform seized white-owned farms; farming output and the economy collapsed.
  • 2008: hyperinflation made the currency worthless.
  • 2017: the army pushed Mugabe out.
sum: Zimbabwe is a landlocked country in southern Africa between the Zambezi and Limpopo rivers. On the map it covers British Southern Rhodesia and the republic that won independence in 1980.
